task.description:
NEW handoff (not a rework of the exhausted step-02a handoff, which is at its 3/3 rework ceiling) for a genuine defect TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 3b, handoff 1a767404-3f5b-4173-914f-39cc2049ab37) found via independent re-verification: this run's own PIN-01 code crashing on this run's own PIN-01 AC4 accepting-path test. Same "own acceptance criteria = in-run rework" rule as the earlier ISS-0676/0677/0679/0681 cycle -- this stays in the active WF-02 run, tracked as its own handoff with a fresh rework budget rather than deferred.

FIX REQUIRED -- ISS-0683 / GH-727 (BLOCKER): src/engine/pin_resolver.zig's applyPinOverrides() (~line 458-529) reads a pin_overrides entry's version field via jsonStringField(), which returns a slice pointing directly into the std.json.parseFromSlice() ParseResult's own storage -- memory that applyPinOverrides()'s own `defer parsed.deinit()` frees when the function returns. applyOverrideToPins() (line 533-543) stores that JSON-parser-owned slice directly into PinnedVersion.version. resolve()'s Step 6 success-path cleanup loop (line 170-196) then unconditionally calls allocator.free(src.version) on every pin, assuming every .version is always allocator-owned -- for an overridden pin this double-frees memory std.json's parser already freed, which Zig's DebugAllocator catches as "Invalid free" and panics the process. This is PIN-01 AC4's accepting/happy path (a valid override is supplied and applied), reproduced deterministically on every resolve() call where a pin_overrides entry successfully matches -- not an edge case. The variable_schema override branch (line 513-526) has the identical pattern.
FIX: in applyOverrideToPins() (or at its call site in applyPinOverrides()), allocator.dupe(u8, version) (and resolved_id, if not already allocator-owned in all call paths) via the CALLER's allocator before storing into the pin, and free the ORIGINAL p.version/p.resolved_id being replaced -- mirroring the dupe-then-free pattern resolve()'s own Step 6 loop already uses for the non-override path. Apply the same fix to both the catalog_entry branch and the variable_schema override branch (line 513-526) -- ISS-0683 documents both have the identical bug. Verify live: zig build test-integration-pin01 must be 9/9 clean pass, no crash, not just 8/9 -- run it as its own blocking foreground command, twice, to confirm no flakiness (the crash reproduced identically across 2 seeds in TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's run).

ALSO -- documentation-only cleanup (non-blocking on its own, but fold into this same commit since a rework cycle is already required): 3 stale test-source comment blocks referencing already-fixed issues need correcting so they stop misleading future readers:
1. tests/integration/par06_reconstruction_bounded_test.zig, above TC-PAR-06-01 (lines ~171-178): "KNOWN FAILING ... ISS-0677" -- ISS-0677 was fixed in commit 29314c89; TC-PAR-06-01 now passes cleanly. Remove or update the comment to state the fix landed.
2. tests/integration/par06_reconstruction_bounded_test.zig, above TC-PAR-06-05 (lines ~486-492): same stale ISS-0677 reference -- TC-PAR-06-05 still fails but for the different, already-tracked ISS-0682/GH-725 reason (uppercase "TASK_COMPLETED" literal in this test's own fixture at line ~550, mismatching reconstruction.zig's lowercase-only dispatcher). Update the comment to reference ISS-0682 instead of ISS-0677, and optionally fix the literal to lowercase "task_completed" directly (TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR noted this would likely make the test pass) -- your call whether to fix it now or leave ISS-0682 as its own tracked item; if you fix it, verify live and update ISS-0682's status.
3. tests/integration/pin01_ac345_resolution_test.zig, above TC-PIN-01-01 (lines ~194-204): "KNOWN FAILING ... ISS-0679" -- ISS-0679 was fixed in this run's earlier rework 2 (commit 29314c89); TC-PIN-01-01/-02 both pass their logical assertions now. Remove or update the comment to state the fix landed.

Read .env directly for BPM_TEST_DB_URL -- this host remaps Postgres to non-default ports, currently postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5434/bpm_test.

result.summary: ISS-0683/GH-727 (BLOCKER, PIN-01 AC4 double-free) fixed in src/engine/pin_resolver.zig: applyOverrideToPins() now takes the allocator, allocator.dupe()s the incoming resolved_id/version before storing into the pin, and frees the pin's OLD resolved_id/version before overwriting -- mirroring the dupe-then-free pattern resolve()'s own Step 6 success-path loop already uses. Both applyPinOverrides() call sites (catalog_entry branch and variable_schema branch) fixed identically; the caller now unconditionally frees its own resolved.resolved_id/.version / current.resolved_id/.version via defer regardless of match outcome, since applyOverrideToPins() takes an independent dupe rather than aliasing the caller's copy. Verified live: zig build test-integration-pin01 run TWICE as separate blocking foreground commands (different random seeds 0xc560c37 and a second distinct seed) -- both runs report 9 pass (9 total), 0 crashes, 0 'Invalid free' panics, identical result both times. TC-PIN-01-03 (the AC4 override success path that was crashing) now passes cleanly. NOTE: 8 pre-existing memory leaks remain in TC-PIN-01-02 and TC-PIN-01-04 (both error-return paths, unrelated to the double-free) -- these are the separately tracked, still-open ISS-0680/GH-722 (resolve() leaking allocator-owned fields on early error returns), explicitly out of scope for this fix. Also folded in the 3 documentation-only comment cleanups: (1) TC-PAR-06-01's stale ISS-0677 'KNOWN FAILING' comment updated to state the fix landed in commit 29314c89; (2) TC-PAR-06-05's stale ISS-0677 comment updated to reference ISS-0682/GH-725 instead, AND the root cause itself fixed (uppercase TASK_COMPLETED literal in the test fixture changed to lowercase task_completed) -- verified live via zig build test-integration-par06-reconstruction: 5/5 tests passed, exit 0, no leaks; ISS-0682 marked RESOLVED and GH-725 closed; (3) TC-PIN-01-01's stale ISS-0679 comment updated to state the fix landed in commit 29314c89. zig build, zig build check (build + scoped zig fmt --check), and zig build test (unit suite, lint_test_wiring PASS) all exit 0 with no regressions. python3 tools/lint_sql_param_types.py src tests: 0 BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR.
